---
title: "Mixed Models & BLUP"
---

## TL;DR

::: {.callout-tip}
The linear mixed model $\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{Xb} + \mathbf{Zu} +
\mathbf{e}$ with $\mathbf{u} \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{K}\sigma_u^2)$
is the workhorse behind every prediction routine in `masreml`. **BLUP**
("best linear unbiased prediction") is the conditional expectation
$E[\mathbf{u} \mid \mathbf{y}]$, computed in practice by solving
Henderson's mixed-model equations. The choice of $\mathbf{K}$ —
pedigree $\mathbf{A}$, SNP-based $\mathbf{G}$, or microhaplotype-based
$\mathbf{G}_{\text{mh}}$ — yields A-BLUP, GBLUP, or MH-GBLUP
respectively.
:::

## The model

$$
\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{Xb} + \mathbf{Zu} + \mathbf{e}
$$ {#eq-mixed-model}

where:

- $\mathbf{y}$ is the $n \times 1$ vector of phenotypes,
- $\mathbf{X}$ is the $n \times p$ design matrix of fixed-effect covariates,
- $\mathbf{b}$ is the $p \times 1$ vector of fixed effects,
- $\mathbf{Z}$ is the $n \times q$ design matrix mapping observations to random-effect levels (often $\mathbf{Z} = \mathbf{I}$ when one observation per individual),
- $\mathbf{u}$ is the $q \times 1$ vector of random additive genetic effects,
- $\mathbf{e}$ is the $n \times 1$ residual vector.

The standard distributional assumptions are

$$
\mathbf{u} \sim N\bigl(\mathbf{0},\, \mathbf{K}\sigma_u^2\bigr), \quad
\mathbf{e} \sim N\bigl(\mathbf{0},\, \mathbf{I}\sigma_e^2\bigr), \quad
\mathrm{Cov}(\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{e}) = \mathbf{0},
$$ {#eq-mvn}

so $\mathrm{Var}(\mathbf{y}) = \mathbf{Z}\mathbf{K}\mathbf{Z}^\top \sigma_u^2 + \mathbf{I}\sigma_e^2$.
$\mathbf{K}$ is the **relationship matrix**; its definition is what
distinguishes one BLUP variant from another (pedigree $\mathbf{A}$ for
A-BLUP, $\mathbf{G}$ for [GBLUP](gblup-gwablup.qmd)).

## Assumptions

1. **Linearity** in the fixed and random effects — non-linear genetic
   architectures are absorbed into the relationship matrix or pushed to
   [Bayesian alternatives](bayesian-alphabet.qmd).
2. **Multivariate normality** of $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{e}$.
3. **Homoscedastic residuals** — $\mathrm{Var}(\mathbf{e}) = \mathbf{I}\sigma_e^2$. Heteroscedasticity by family / population / sex requires structured residual variance.
4. **Independence between $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{e}$**.
5. **$\mathbf{K}$ is correctly specified** — wrong allele coding,
   omitted dominance, or pedigree errors enter through $\mathbf{K}$ and
   bias BLUP toward shrinkage.

When binary traits or other non-Gaussian responses break assumption 2,
move to the [Threshold Model](threshold-model.qmd).

## BLUP solution

Henderson's mixed-model equations (MME) are

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
\mathbf{X}^\top \mathbf{X} & \mathbf{X}^\top \mathbf{Z} \\
\mathbf{Z}^\top \mathbf{X} & \mathbf{Z}^\top \mathbf{Z} + \mathbf{K}^{-1} \lambda
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} \hat{\mathbf{b}} \\ \hat{\mathbf{u}} \end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{X}^\top \mathbf{y} \\ \mathbf{Z}^\top \mathbf{y} \end{bmatrix},
$$ {#eq-mme}

with the **variance ratio** $\lambda = \sigma_e^2 / \sigma_u^2$. Solving
@eq-mme directly gives both $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ (GLS estimates of the
fixed effects) and $\hat{\mathbf{u}} = E[\mathbf{u} \mid \mathbf{y}]$
in one pass — this is the "best linear unbiased prediction" property:
$\hat{\mathbf{u}}$ minimises mean-squared error among all linear,
unbiased predictors.

Variance components $(\sigma_u^2, \sigma_e^2)$ are typically estimated
by **REML** (restricted / residual maximum likelihood), then plugged
back into @eq-mme. `masreml::masreml()` does both steps in one call.

## When to use

| Situation | Best fit |
|---|---|
| Continuous trait, polygenic architecture | A-BLUP or GBLUP via `masreml(y, markers = list(snp_add = X))` |
| Continuous trait, $p \gg n$ markers | GBLUP — see [GBLUP & GWABLUP](gblup-gwablup.qmd) |
| Sparse architecture (few large-effect QTL) | Bayesian alternatives — see [Bayesian Alphabet](bayesian-alphabet.qmd) |
| Binary trait | `masreml(y, markers = ..., trait = "binary", link = "logit")` — see [Threshold model](threshold-model.qmd) |
| Pre-built relationship matrix (e.g. pedigree A) | `masreml(y, G = list(snp_add = G_mat))` |
| Need per-marker effect inference | GWAS (`masreml::run_gwas`) or BayesR variable selection |
